title: Being refused bank loans for Dover Records
summary: Despite twenty years in business, banks would not lend for Dover Records in the mid-sixties; he borrowed from loan sharks and lost about $300,000 when it collapsed.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: You know. Well, and that gets back to another problem that you seem to have always had. Uh, uh, we, we talked, talked about just why, why were there record companies in this town? Well, there was no capital. There was the capital that was with those people in the upside. They wouldn't, wouldn't touch you with a very real ten-footer. Right.

Right. Yeah. But, you know, as late, as late as the middle sixties, when I started Dover and it started to be successful, I couldn't get a penny from banks. I actually went to banks because by the time we got real busy, we had a telex machine and the orders would come in on the telexes. And I actually went to banks with a handful of telexes and said, these are orders. All I want to borrow is the money it takes to produce the record until I can collect one.
No way. You had a fairly good track record. I mean, you had a successful studio.
I had, yeah, well, I, I'd been in business by that time 20 years. 20 years? You know, and not exactly a newcomer.
But you must have had some ongoing arrangements in some bank when it had the studio. No.
Okay. By the time I started Dover records, I owned seven or eight pieces of real estate. I was a little double houses or whatever. I had a mortgage, but I owned a studio building.

Couldn't borrow money to remodel the building. Couldn't borrow money to, to buy the pressing machines. And I had to cut deals with people in Latin. And, and, and I had to borrow money from loan shop types.

So when Dover collapsed as a, as an operation, I never, ever went into bankruptcy as such. But when it collapsed as an operation, I lost all of that. I lost in 1965 dollars about 300,000 dollars of my own money. And it was because of the way it was set up. And I was liable for all of it. You know? Mm-hmm. And it was a, it was a financial disaster for me.
